ModuleName: Version Control, GitHub Pages, and Course Repository Integration

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: An outline of all topics covered in this module, listing the key lessons on Git repository management, GitHub Pages publishing, the Course Repository Service, archive export, iFrame embedding, and choosing a sharing method, used by learners and instructors to preview module scope and navigate to specific sections.

Artifacts.Name: Managing a Course as a Git Repository in PreseMaker
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains how PreseMaker integrates Git version control directly into its interface, walking learners through initializing a repository, committing changes with a message, and pushing changes to a remote repository without needing a terminal.

Artifacts.Name: Publishing a Course Website with GitHub Pages
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains how to publish a completed PreseMaker course as a publicly accessible website using GitHub Pages, covering how to export the course, connect it to a GitHub repository, and trigger publishing from within PreseMaker rather than through GitHub's website.

Artifacts.Name: Using the Course Repository Service
Artifacts.Description: A reading that describes PreseMaker's built-in integration with an external Course Repository Service, explaining how educators can browse, share, upload, and reuse course materials with colleagues directly from within the application.

Artifacts.Name: Other Sharing Options: Archive Export and iFrame Embedding
Artifacts.Description: A reading that covers two additional course distribution options in PreseMaker — exporting a course as a downloadable archive file and embedding a course into another webpage using an iFrame — explaining when and how to use each method.

Artifacts.Name: Choosing the Right Sharing Method
Artifacts.Description: A reading that compares all five sharing and distribution methods available in PreseMaker, helping learners and instructors decide which approach best fits their workflow, audience, and technical environment.
